Jobs that don't exist anymore: Home ice delivery, 1942. The block of ice would go into your "ice box" to keep your food cold. Replaced by the refrigerator.
Home Ice delivery still exists in some third world countries.

My grandfather, who I worked with just this day, had this as his first job ever. He started when he was 15 and while he was out on delivery once he turned 16, went by the sheriff's office and was handwritten a driver's license.

Theres a few interesting facts about home ice delivery, that block of ice shown in the picture being delivered could have been cut from ice almost a year before hand and from several hundred if not a couple thousand miles way. There was an international trade from places like Northern Canada to the UK and even as far as North America to Australia hauling nothing but frozen water for consumers and during the voyage they may only lose a fifth of the ice to melting. When the refrigerator started to take over the ice hauling companies tried to start a campaign to discredit the fridge as a bogus technology vastly inferior to natural ice, that the items frozen and chilled in it would spoil earlier.

Bonus mostly useless fact, a freezer is just a fridge within a fridge.

Useless trivia: This company is based out of Troy, New York. While the ice may have been old (based on his summer attire), it likely did not travel very far as the area, and all of the upper Hudson river Valley were a major harvesting site.
I remember reading about how some of those companies still exist today as ice, dry ice, and chill haulage companies.
